Da vs D.K. Chhatwal Etc on 21 March, 2018

1.
The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 195
4 (herein after referred to as PFA Act),
alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 03.07.2001 the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh Gian Chand, FI Pawan Bhatnagar alongwith staff and under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM Sh R.K. Ahuja visited the premises of M/s Princess Garden Restaurant Pvt Ltd, E-32, NDSE Part II, New Delhi, where the accused No. 1 D.K. Chhatwal was found conducting the business of above said shop, including Oyster Sauce, ready for use in preparation of Chinese food for sale for human consumption.
The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Oyster Sauce from the vendor for analysis.
The sample consisted of 3 original sealed bottles of 180 oz each of Oyster Sauce having identical label declaration was taken.
The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh R.K. Ahuja SDM/LHA.

The FI divided the sample of the article of food into three equal parts by putting one original sealed bottle in one counterpart and each counter part containing the sample of Olyster Sauce was DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc separately, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act &
Rules.
The vendor's signature were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottle.
Notice was given to the accused D.K. Chhatwal and the price of the sample was also given to him vide receipt dated 03.07.2001.
Panchanama was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by FI were signed by the accused D.K. Chhatwal as well as the witness Sh Pawan Bhatnagar FI.
Before taking sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward.
3. One counterpart of the sample was sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter parts of the sample were deposited in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be misbranded.

The report of the PA is as follows :-
"The sample is misbranded as there is violation of Rule 32 (b)(c)(e)(f)(i) and Rule 33".
4.

It is further the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 D.K. Chhatwal is the vendor of accused No. 2 M/s Princess Garden Restaurant Pvt Ltd, E-32, NDSE Part-II, New Delhi at the time of sampling.

Accused No. 2 M/s Princess Garden Restaurant Pvt having two Directors i.e. A.L. Kholi and Sandeep Kholi and the company had nominated accused No. 3 Yam Dutt as its nominee as per PFA Act as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of vendor company.

It is further stated that vendor firm M/s Princess Garden Restaurant Pvt purchased the sample commodity from accused No. 4 M/s Northern Traders vide Bill No. 2465 dated 30.06.2001 and said DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc firm is a proprietorship firm having two partners i.e. accused No.
5 S.C. Ahuja and Mrs., Suman Ahuja. Accused No. 5 S.C. Ahuja is the main partner as per STO reply dated 20.09.2001 and is responsible for day to day conduct of the firm M/s Northern Traders.

It is further stated that accused No. 4 M/s Northern Traders purchased the sample commodity from M/s Vijaya Enterprises, 10123, Library Road, Azad Market, Delhi -6 vide invoice No. 13802 dated 15.06.2001.

M/s Vijaya Enterprises is a proprietorship firm under the proprietorship of accused No.
6 Vijay Kumar Dhawan.

3 5.

It is further stated that M/s Vijaya Enterprises has purchased the sample commodity from accused No. 7 M/s Paramount Traders, which is a partnership firm and having three partners i.e.
accused No. 8 K.L. Dhawan, accused No. 9 Vijay Dhawan and accused No. 10 Vinod Kumar Dhawan.
The said firm had no nominee as per PFA Act as such all the three partners are incharge of and responsible to the conduct of the firm.

It is further stated that accused No. 7 M/s Paramount Traders,had purchased the sample commodity from the importer i.e. accused No. 11 M/s Kalra Trading Co. which is a partnership firm and accused No. 12 Rajesh Kalra and accused No. 13 Praveen Kalra are the partners of the said firm.

It is further stated that accused No. 11 M/s Kalra Trading Co. imported the sample commodity from M/s Pal Trading Co. Thailand vide bill No.
P-014/2000 dated 11.05.2001 and no evidence has been collected against them so far by the investigation agency as such they have not been made as delinquent party.
DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc 6.
Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 11.04.2002 alleging violation of section 2(ix) (k) of PFA Act read with Rule 33 and also Rule 32 (b)(c)(e)(f)(i) of PFA Rules, as punishable section 7/16(1)
(a) of PFA Act against the accused persons.
7. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 11.04.2002.

Based on the report of the PA as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 33 and also Rule 32 (b)
(c)(e)(f)(i) of PFA Rules, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

During the trial,
proceedings against the accused No. 1 D.K. Chhatwal & accused No. 8 K.L. Dhawan were abated and accused No. 3 was declared proclaimed offender.
The accused No. 2, 4,5,6,7, 9 & 10 were also discharged vide order dated 15.04.2013 in the present case.
8. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 LHA Sh R.K.Ahuja, PW-2 FI Gian Chand and PW-3 FI Pawan Bhatnagar.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand and PW-3 FI Pawan Bhatnagar were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh R.K.Ahuja.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc sample of 3x18 oz sealed bottle of Oyster Sauce imported from Thailand in original sealed condition bearing identical label declaration,
dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting one original sealed bottle of Oyster Sauce in one counterpart and each containing the sample of Oyster Sauce was separately sealing,
packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B,
Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C.

The vendor disclosed the source of purchase of sample commodity from Da vs D.K. Chhatwal Etc on 21 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184178917/
4 M/s Northern Traders, 88 Rajender Nagar Market vide invoice Mark-X.
A Notice under Section 14 A Ex.PW1/D was also prepared at the spot addressed to M/s Northern Traders, 88 Rajender Nagar Market.

Thereafter, two counterpart of the sample was deposited in intact condition with LHA on the next working day i.e. 04.07.2001 vide receipt Ex.PW1/E with the intimation that one counter part of the sample has already been deposited in intact condition with PA.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW-1/G was received according to which sample was found misbranded.
Thereafter during the investigation PW-2 FI Gian Chand sent letter Ex.PW2/A to vendor and received reply Ex.PW2/A1 alongwith document Mark A2 & A3.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/B to STO Ward No. 97 and received reply stating that Sh Sandeep Kohli was the Director and A.L. Kholi was the Managing Director of the company.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/C to DHO but no reply was received.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/D to accused Yamdutt, nominee of the accused no. 2 firm.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/E to Norther Traders and DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc received reply Ex.PW2/F alongwith document ark A4 & A5.

sentences.text: PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/H to DHO, MCD to confirm whether any health licence was issued to M/s Northern Traders but no reply was received.

Thereafter, PW-2 FI Gian Chand sent letter Ex.PW2/I to M/s Vijaya Enterprises and received reply Ex.PW2/I1 alognwith document mark A6 &
A7.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/J to STO Ward No. 38 and received reply stating that Vijay Kumar Dhwan was the proprietor.
He also sent letter Ex.PW2/J1 to DHO but no reply was received.
He also sent letter Ex.PW2/K to M/s Paramount Traders and received reply Ex.PW2/K1.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter to STO Ward No. 38 to disclose the constitution of M/s Paramount Traders and received its reply stating that there are three partners of the firm.
PW-2 FI
Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.PW2/M to M/s Kalra Trading Co and received reply Ex.PW2/M1 alongwith invoice A8.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also sent letter Ex.Pw2/N to STO Ward No. 44 to disclose the constitution of M/s Kalra Trading Company and as per reply Ex.Pw2/N1, there were two partners of the said company.
PW-2 FI Gian Chand also received letter Ex.PW2/O from M/s Norther Traders alongwith photocopy of partnership deed Mark A9.

After completion of investigation the entire case file was put before the concerned SDM/LHA who forwarded the same to the then Director of PFA for obtaining the sanction and the then Director PFA after going through the same gave his consent for prosecution Ex.PW-1/H.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex. PW-1/I was filed in the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex. PW1/J alongwith copy of PA Reports were sent to accused persons through LHA through post vide receipt Ex.PW1/K.

The accused DA vs D.K.
Chhatwal etc persons were also served by PW-2 FI Gian Chand and placed on record his report Ex.PW1/J1.

sentences.text: The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel.
9. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 21.07.2014 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
The accused has not led any defence evidence.
10. In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
11. The prosecution alleges the offence of misbranding.

Regarding misbranding the defence has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State Da vs D.K. Chhatwal Etc on 21 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184178917/
5 2009(1) FAC 132 to argue that there was a policy of the complainant department of 1985 numbered as Policy No F6(228)/85/ENF/PFA wherein a decision was taken to give a written warning to the offenders with regard to any deficiency in respect of Rule 32 of the PFA Act.

entities.text: S.S. Gokul Krishanan & Others vs State Da vs D.K. Chhatwal Etc on 21 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although this policy was withdrawn by order No. 5/07 dated 14.09.2007 but since this case was filed April 2002, the accused are covered by aforesaid policy.

Although, no such policy has been placed or proved on record by other side and this policy was further withdrawn as per the aforesaid judgment on the ground that Section 20 of the PFA Act does not confer any such power on the consenting authority to issue such warning to the vendors found violating Rule 32 of the DA vs D.K. Chhatwal etc PFA Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011 and recently in Hello Minerals Water PVT LTD & Ors vs State CRL.MC.224/2016 dated 10.01.2018.
12.

entities.text: M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State & Another Crl.MC 439/2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Hello Minerals Water PVT LTD & Ors vs State CRL.MC.224/2016 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Be that as it may, PFA Act or Rules does not provide any such warning but since the benefit of this policy has been given in the case of S.S. Gokul Krishnan (referred above), I feel myself bound by the ratio of that case.
It is not the case of the prosecution that the accused is not the first offender or that he has already availed the benefit of warning.

13. On the basis of the aforesaid discussion, the accused no.12, Rajesh Kalra also representing accused no.11, Kalra Trading Company, accused no.13 Praveen Kalra and accused no. 3 Yam Dutt who is a proclaimed offender are acquitted of the charges.
